notes.3: The envelope sender, derived from the user-supplied From address.
notes.4: Only act if a sender was set.
notes.6: Builds the extra-parameters string for sendmail, escaping the sender with escapeshellcmd.

options.label: `escapeshellcmd` does not quote spaces, so a crafted Sender injects extra sendmail options (e.g. `-X` to write a file), which can drop a PHP webshell
sendmail is slow, so a flood of messages backs up the queue
options.whyWrong: Throughput is unrelated; the flaw is argument injection into the sendmail command.

options.label: The From address can be spoofed, enabling phishing emails
options.whyWrong: Spoofing is a lesser concern than injecting sendmail arguments that write files.

options.label: Remove semicolons from $sender
options.whyWrong: The attack uses spaces and option tokens like `-X`/`-O`, not semicolons.

options.label: Validate $sender is a well-formed email address (no spaces or option-like tokens) and refuse it otherwise
Base64-encode $sender before using it
options.whyWrong: sendmail won't accept an encoded address and this doesn't stop a crafted plaintext address from being used elsewhere.

training.exploit: Set the From address so the derived Sender is like `"attacker\" -oQueueDirectory=/tmp -X/var/www/html/x.php foo@evil.com"`. `escapeshellcmd` leaves the spaces intact, so sendmail parses `-X/var/www/html/x.php` and writes a log file — containing the attacker-chosen email body with PHP code — to the web root, giving a webshell and remote code execution.

hints.line: The flaw is how the sender is escaped before reaching sendmail.
hints.bugClass: Extra arguments are injected into a command.
hints.why: Does escapeshellcmd stop a value from becoming additional CLI options?
hints.fix: Reject anything that isn't a clean email address.

writeup.summary: PHP's `mail()` passes its 5th argument onto sendmail's command line. `escapeshellcmd` neutralizes shell metacharacters but does not quote spaces, so a Sender crafted with spaces and sendmail options (`-O`, `-X`) becomes extra command-line arguments. `-X` makes sendmail write a log file — including attacker-controlled message content — to a web-accessible path, producing a PHP webshell and remote code execution. The fix validates that the sender is a well-formed address before use (and quotes it), rejecting values that carry option tokens.

verifyExempt: Depends on the real sendmail transport and mail() additional_params handling; and more than one offered fix blocks the exploit, so the single-correct-fix execution contract does not apply. Answer key reviewed against the upstream fix.
